evidence.estrutura: Anscombe wrote political philosophy but did not advance a distinctive federal-versus-centralized constitutional program. Keep structural placement moderate.
evidence.representacao: Her public political interventions were acts of conscience within democratic academic society rather than a developed theory of electoral representation. Use a moderate representative-democratic placement.
evidence.poder: Her opposition to intentional killing of civilians and willingness to confront institutional authority over moral principle support strong constraints on state violence and consequentialist power.
evidence.imigracao: No reliable immigration or assimilation doctrine is central to her work. Keep moderate.
evidence.diplomacia: Her famous opposition to honoring Truman over Hiroshima and Nagasaki reflects moral limits on wartime state action rather than a broad diplomacy doctrine.
evidence.intervencao: Her absolute rejection of intentionally killing innocents strongly supports a restrained just-war position and opposition to indiscriminate military intervention.
evidence.economia: Anscombe's major work did not center ownership, redistribution or welfare policy. Keep economic placement moderate.
evidence.controle: No planning-versus-market doctrine is established. Keep moderate.
evidence.comercio: No trade-policy doctrine is established. Keep moderate.
evidence.religiao: A committed Roman Catholic philosopher, Anscombe explicitly defended a theistic moral framework and divine law. This strongly supports a religious moral orientation, though not automatically theocratic government.
evidence.moral: Her opposition to contraception and abortion and her virtue-ethical, Catholic moral commitments strongly support socially traditional positions.
evidence.tecnologia: Her ethical criticism of atomic bombing shows willingness to constrain powerful technologies by moral limits, but she did not reject technology generally. Use a cautious human-centered placement.
